newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Heavy rain hits Ivorian phone links, kills two.
newsitem.headline: Heavy rain hits Ivorian phone links, kills two.

text.p: Heavy rains knocked out many of Ivory Coast's international telephone links for almost two working days and killed at least two people in poor quarters of the commercial capital Abidjan, officials said on Thursday.
A week of heavy rain in Abidjan coupled with a deluge on Wednesday morning flooded an earth station outside the city, cutting off international telephone links via satellite with the outside world.
Links to former colonial power France, via an undersea cable, were unaffected.
Telephone links resumed on Thursday afternoon.

Souleymane Tao, technical director for the national telephone network CI-TELCOM, which was taken over by France Telecom in February, blamed flooding at the Akakro earth station at Bingerville, onetime capital outside Abidjan.
Such problems are not uncommon in Ivory Coast during the annual long rainy season, which runs from May to July.
Last year, flash flooding killed at least 28 people in shantytowns. Many of these have since been demolished and their inhabitants moved.
